---
title: "Study 07 — Collective-variable scoping"
subtitle: "Which CVs to bias in MACE-driven metadynamics — a first pass"
---

Metadynamics needs collective variables to bias along. We compute a battery of
seven candidate CVs on trajectories spanning the distinct states (stable
droplet, fragmenting droplet, big droplet, drifting cluster, monomer
dissociation) and ask which are informative, non-redundant, and capture the
processes we care about.

## What separates the states

Between/within-state variance ratio (higher = more discriminating):

| CV | separation | defined on |
|----|:----------:|:----------:|
| **coord_OO** (O–O coordination) | **50.9** | all |
| **n_hbond_pm** (angular H-bonds/mol) | **12.6** | all |
| asphericity | 4.9 | droplets |
| q_tet (tetrahedral order) | 1.4 | droplets |
| max_OO | 1.0 | all |
| Rg | 1.0 | all |
| max_OH | 0.8 | all |

O–O coordination and the angular H-bond count separate the states best. `max_OH`
scores low only because a single state dissociates — but it's the *only* CV that
fires there, so it's an essential orthogonal chemical coordinate.

## The 7 CVs collapse to ~3 directions

Redundant families (|r| > 0.9): `Rg ≈ max_OO` (size); `coord_OO ≈ n_hbond_pm ≈
−asphericity` (network integrity). PCA: **PC1 (43%) = network integrity**, **PC2
(30%) = size + dissociation** — 73% in two components, and the states separate
cleanly in that plane.

![States in CV space: droplets cluster at high network integrity (left); the
drifting cluster traces a path across as its network breaks; the dissociating
monomer splits off along the O–H axis.](assets/cv_pca.png){width=560}

![CV correlation — the redundancy structure (size family, network
family).](assets/cv_correlation.png){width=440}

## Recommended CV set (minimal, non-redundant)

1. **Network integrity** — mean O–O coordination *or* angular H-bond count (pick one).
2. **Size / spread** — `Rg` (or `max_OO`).
3. **Chemistry** — `max_OH` + a **per-oxygen O–H coordination** for proton transfer.

::: {.callout-important}
## Caveat & next step
This separates *different systems*, so some discriminating power reflects size,
not slow dynamics *within* one droplet. For choosing what to **bias**, the sharper
question — which CV captures the slow reorganization within a single droplet —
needs a **time-lagged analysis (TICA / VAMP)** or a **learned CV** on one system's
trajectory. That's the next step, on top of this physically-motivated shortlist.
:::
